Antigravity CLI vs Claude Code vs Codex: the same Opus 5.5 read 71% to 89% fewer tokens in Antigravity

Measured and written by Jonhisking · Updated 2026-10-23. Disclosure: TokenSave gets no funding, credits or sponsorship from AI companies. All measurements use our own paid subscriptions.

The same model, Claude Opus 5.5, read 71% to 89% fewer input tokens in Google’s Antigravity CLI than in Claude Code for the same coding task, and 71% to 85% fewer before doing anything. Both made a working game. Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity also stayed far below Claude Code and Codex. The range comes from one open question: whether Antigravity’s separately reported cache reads should be added on top.

Measured 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-23 · 52 runs · Claude Code 2.1.295, Codex CLI 0.162, Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 · License CC BY 4.0 · Earlier: Claude Code vs Codex

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23569397 · Also on Hugging Face · Kaggle · GitHub

Key findings

  • Startup: 35,781 input tokens in Claude Code, 14,818 in Codex, 6,745 in Antigravity with Gemini 4 Argon and 5,326 in Antigravity with Opus 5.5 (10,493 counting its cache reads), for the prompt “Reply with the single word OK.” with no MCP server. Most of it is each tool’s own instructions and tool definitions, sent with every request.
  • Same task, same model: asked to build a brick-breaker game, Opus 5.5 read 87,779 input tokens in Claude Code and 9,935 in Antigravity (25,347 counting cache reads), wrote 7,669 and 4,463 output tokens, and took 62 and 43 seconds. Claude Code’s games were longer (474 lines on average against 245). Claude Code put the run at $0.39 at API prices; Antigravity shows no price.
  • Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity read 12,899 input tokens (19,695 counting cache reads) and wrote the longest games (600 lines), but took the longest too (77 seconds). Codex read 52,762 on average (47,954 to 70,704) and wrote minified games of about 58 lines.
  • MCP tools barely matter any more. Thirty test tools added 388 tokens in Claude Code, none in Codex (14,618 in seven of its eight startup runs, with or without tools), 582 in Antigravity with Gemini and 417 with Opus. In Antigravity one tool already added 456 (Gemini) and 278 (Opus) and 29 more added little, so all four now seem to load a tool’s details only when it is used.
  • All 20 games worked in a headless-browser check: the score rises when bricks break, level 2 appears, and lives go 3, 2, 1, 0. The automatic check could not read the score in two Codex games; a manual check showed bricks breaking and points adding up in both.
  • Why Antigravity: Google stopped serving Gemini CLI to personal accounts (Google AI Pro, Ultra and free Code Assist) on 2026-06-18 and pointed them to Antigravity CLI. Antigravity can also run Claude models, which is what makes the same-model comparison possible.

The same coding task

“Make a brick-breaker game that runs in the browser as a single file named index.html … 2 levels, a score display and 3 lives … keyboard and mouse.” Average of five runs each, medium effort. How to read Antigravity’s numbers

agy --output-format json reports input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, cache_read_tokens and total_tokens, where total is input plus output. Its documentation does not say whether cache reads are part of input. In our Opus runs the cache reads (15,412 on the game task) were larger than the reported input (9,935), so there they cannot be contained in it. We therefore show both: the reported input as the low figure and input plus cache reads as the high one. Even the high figure is far below Claude Code’s.

Method

  • Windows 11, 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-23. Every run in its own empty folder, one after another, with no other MCP servers.
  • Claude Code 2.1.295, Opus 5.5, Max plan: claude -p --output-format json --mcp-config mcp.json --strict-mcp-config; the game at --effort medium --permission-mode acceptEdits. Input = input + cache creation + cache read.
  • Codex CLI 0.162.0-alpha.17.2, gpt-6-luna, ChatGPT plan: codex exec --json, reasoning effort low for startup and medium for the game, MCP server added with -c mcp_servers.…. Input includes cached input.
  • Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 (agy), personal Google account: agy -p --output-format json --model gemini-4-argon-medium or claude-opus-5-5-medium; the game with --mode accept-edits. The MCP server was written to the global ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json for each startup run and removed afterwards.
  • MCP test server: the same small stdio server as in our Claude Code vs Codex dataset, exposing 1, 10 or 30 tracker tools with a one-sentence description and a five-field schema each.
  • Games were checked in headless Chromium: break bricks and watch the score, clear or skip to level 2, and lose the ball until lives reach zero. Scripts and every log are in the GitHub mirror.

Limitations

  • Two runs per startup test and five per game, on three days with the same tool versions. One task, one machine.
  • Token counts are each tool’s own report, and the three tools count cache differently (see above). Prices are not compared: Codex and Antigravity show none on a subscription.
  • We cannot see how Antigravity sets up Opus 5.5 behind its claude-opus-5-5-medium name, so its settings may differ from Claude Code’s medium effort.
